summary.headline: Shree Cement Q1 FY27 consol operational EBITDA fell to INR1,272 crore (1,111/t vs 1,339/t) on volume of 114.5 lakh t, as fuel switch and lower clinker factor hit costs.
summary.overview: Management asked analysts to shift to consolidated reporting (India plus UAE and other subsidiaries), citing ~10% of turnover from overseas and non-standalone businesses. Q1 was hit by the Middle East war: petcoke share fell from 54% to 9% and coal rose to 81% from 32%, while Omani gypsum did not arrive, raising fuel cost to about INR1.95/kcal and lowering the clinker conversion factor to 1.50 from 1.58. Trade mix fell to 62% from 71% and blended to 60% from 70%, which management attributes to a weaker conversion factor pushing more OPC into non-trade. Management says fuel cost has peaked and guides to better Q2 onwards, with FY27 volume target of 40 million tonnes reiterated.

segments.name: India grey cement (standalone)
segments.commentary: Capacity utilisation 62% overall (North 66%, East 60%, South 57%), flat YoY on a larger base. South sales rose from 11 lakh t to ~16.9 lakh t, North grew ~20%, East was flat; Q1 India volume about 10.4-10.5 million t.

segments.name: UAE (Ras Al Khaimah)
segments.commentary: No meaningful sales in April and May due to the war, which dragged consolidated volume. Capacity doubling is underway to about 7 million t by Q3 FY27, funded from UAE cash; management declined to disclose UAE EBITDA or revenue.

segments.name: RMC
segments.commentary: 26 operational plants versus 19 at start of year, with 8 added in Q1 and 10 more planned next quarter. Management says RMC is EBITDA-neutral at present, targeting about 5% margin over time.

segments.name: Northeast (Assam/Meghalaya) greenfield
segments.commentary: Plant planned for Q4 FY28 with 1 million t first phase and infrastructure for 4-5 million t; management says all approvals are in place.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume target maintained at 40 million t (India); H1 FY27 expected at about 19.5-20 million t (Q1 about 10.4-10.5 million t, Q2 guided at 9-9.5 million t).
Fuel cost has peaked at about INR1.95/kcal and should stay broadly stable barring Middle East escalation; packing cost and PVC prices have started easing.
Management expects healthier profitability from Q2 onward but does not give EBITDA guidance; cites 3.1 million t sold in July 2026 as of 31 July.
Trade/non-trade mix expected to normalise gradually; long-term aim is 70% trade, 30% non-trade, with conversion factor recovery as the lever.
FY27 capex guidance of about INR1,500 crore for India operations; FY28 capex to be given next quarter. Depreciation FY27 INR2,400-2,500 crore; tax rate about 30%.
Standalone share of consolidated revenue expected to fall from 88-89% to 75-80% over about five years.
capex_capacity: India capex of INR456 crore in Q1 FY27 against full-year guidance of about INR1,500 crore.
UAE (Ras Al Khaimah) capacity doubling, with output to reach about 7 million t by Q3 FY27, funded from UAE cash flows.
Northeast greenfield plant to commission in Q4 FY28: 1 million t initial phase, site built for 4-5 million t; limestone available in region.
Renewable energy share of total energy rose to 66% from 61%; ~100 electric commercial vehicles to be commissioned this year; BESS piloted on a small scale.
Rail share of dispatches about 9% in Q1; railway sidings under Gati Shakti being pursued.
demand_pricing: Industry demand expected to grow 7-8% pan-India; Shree aims for about 10%. FY26 volume was 35.4 million t versus 40 million t FY27 target.
East demand reported as up ~20% incrementally; Shree East volume flat YoY, constrained by conversion factor and coal quality.
Realisation of INR4,919/t vs INR4,854/t YoY; management says the gap to peers has narrowed to roughly INR10-12/bag but did not improve in Q1.
Premium sales hit by higher non-trade mix; management declined to give pricing guidance.
Sales push into Maharashtra and Gujarat, served by the South plant.

qa_highlights.question: What were blended fuel cost, trade mix, clinker factor and realisation in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Fuel cost INR1.95/kcal; trade mix 62% (vs 71%), blended 60% (vs 70%); clinker factor 1.50 (vs 1.58); realisation INR4,919/t vs INR4,854/t a year earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 fuel cost rise further?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects fuel cost to be broadly flat at INR1.95/kcal, with at most a INR0.02-0.03 increase, provided Middle East stays calm.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the mix shift to non-trade?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower-quality coal raised clinker ash absorption and cut the conversion factor, leaving more OPC, which sells mainly into non-trade. Management expects normalisation over time, not a permanent change.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR200 crore non-standalone EBITDA comes from UAE, and what are UAE EBITDA/revenue per tonne?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to split EBITDA or revenue for UAE or other subsidiaries and asked analysts to model consolidated figures only.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Northeast plant economics given capex per tonne?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR1,800 crore figure relates to 1 million t of a 4-5 million t site, not a standalone 1 million t project, and that it will proceed in learning steps.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any inorganic growth plan given net cash?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said it is not pursuing acquisitions and will not buy capacity at about $110/t capex for $5 EBITDA/t assets.

risks_watch: Middle East escalation could reverse the fuel and gypsum cost relief and disrupt the Oman gypsum and petcoke supply.
Trade mix recovery from 62% to the historical 70%; monitor the conversion factor path back above 1.50.
Reporting shift to consolidated numbers with limited disclosure of UAE and subsidiary EBITDA, revenue and capex; consol capex guidance still pending.
UAE volumes depend on war-affected sales resuming and on the capacity doubling to 7 million t by Q3 FY27.
Northeast plant permits and logistics; management says approvals are in place but local protests were reported in media.
summary.management_tone: Defensive on Q1 and evasive on consolidated segment figures, with repeated requests to treat Q1 as an abnormal quarter. Confident on fuel cost having peaked and on the 40 million t volume target, but declined to guide on price or EBITDA.
key_quotes: Please consider Q1 as an abnormal quarter. I expect to do better Q2 onwards, if nothing untoward happens on Middle East front.

time has probably come when we should look at consolidated numbers instead of standalone.
